turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from device physics and training patterns

**What the training data says about high-efficiency p-i-n MAPbI₃ stacks:**

1. **PTAA as HTL with fullerene/BCP ETLs and Cu back contacts** dominates the high end: PCBM-60|C60|BCP / PTAA / Cu = 18.85%; C60|BCP / PTAA / Cu = 18.62–19.09%. PTAA gives a deep HOMO well-aligned to MAPbI₃, low interface recombination, and Cu is a low-cost, well-matched electron-blocking back contact.

2. **Plasmonic/passivated NiO-c**: "Au-np | NiO-c" reaches **20.0%** — Au nanoparticles improve NiO conductivity/extraction and light management; modified NiO-c (SDBS 19.04, [BMIM]BF₄-modified PCBM on NiO-c 21.33) consistently tops the list.

3. **PTAA | PMMA passivation** with PCBM|Bphen and Al hit **19.48%** — PMMA passivates the perovskite/HTL interface.

4. **ITCPTC-type non-fullerene acceptor + C60|BCP on P3CT-Na**: the thiophene analog gives **18.49%** (vs. 16.4% with Rhodamine/LiF instead of C60|BCP), so the Se analog with C60|BCP should perform similarly.

5. **Doctor blading with C60|BCP/Cu** works well (18.4% with no HTL; 16.9% with PTAA/Ag) — scalable coating doesn't hurt when the contact stack is right.

**Mapping to candidates:**

- **c038** (PCBM-60|PEI / Au-np|NiO-c / Ag): near-replica of the 20.0% plasmonic NiO device, with PEI dipole layer further lowering the cathode-side barrier → best bet.
- **c030** (IDTT2FPDI|PCBM-60|Bphen / PTAA|PMMA / Al): direct analog of the 19.48% PMMA-passivated PTAA cell, with an added NFA interlayer for trap passivation.
- **c044** (PCBM-60|BCP / PTAA / Cu, spin-coating): matches the 18.6–18.9% PTAA/Cu family exactly.
- **c097** (ITCPTC-Se|C60|BCP / P3CT-Na / Ag): Se analog of the 18.49% ITCPTC-Th device with the superior C60|BCP interlayer (clearly better than the Rhodamine/LiF variant, so preferred over c063).
- **c088** (C60|BCP / PTAA / Cu, doctor blading on willow glass|ITO): combines the best contact stack (PTAA/Cu, 18.6–19.1%) with a blading process shown to give ~18.4% in this family.

Runners-up considered but ranked lower: c034/c072 (PTAA with Al, slightly worse than Cu), c085 (PTAA/Ag ~17.2%), c035/c066 (TEAX|PCBM|PEI/NiO-c ~15.3%), c009/c083/c021 (C60-derivative|BCP/NiO-c ~14.5%).

Final: c038, c030, c044, c097, c088
